narrative:
Based on the analysis of your academic profile, the system estimates a 47% chance that you will fail your final year. Because this exceeds the 10% threshold used to identify students who need additional support, you are required to take remedial courses.

The single strongest factor driving this prediction is your history of past failures. Unlike students who are not required to take remedial courses, who on average have no prior failures, you have one previous class failure on record. This significantly increases the likelihood of struggling again and is by far the most influential reason behind this decision.

Two other factors were also considered, though they worked in your favour and partially offset the concern above. Your family size — being three or fewer people at home — was associated with a slightly lower risk of failing, perhaps reflecting a more focused home environment. Similarly, your weekly study time of two to five hours also nudged the prediction in a positive direction, suggesting you are putting in a reasonable effort compared to many of your peers.

However, these positive signals were not strong enough to outweigh the concern raised by your academic history.

The good news is that your situation is far from hopeless. You have expressed a desire to pursue higher education, you have internet access at home, and you are already dedicating time to studying. The remedial courses are designed to build on these strengths and help you address the gaps that led to your previous failure. Engaging actively with this additional support gives you a genuine opportunity to turn things around.
